answer: Under the Good Cause Eviction Law, a landlord may seek in good faith to recover possession of a housing accommodation for their own personal use or for the personal use of specified family members, including a child, as their principal residence, provided that no other suitable housing accommodation in the building is available. To do this, the landlord must establish this good faith by clear and convincing evidence. However, this ground does not apply if you are sixty-five years of age or older or if you are a disabled person. If you are required to surrender your apartment due to a fraudulent statement regarding this proposed use, you have a right to bring a court action for damages and relief. Because I am not a lawyer, I cannot give legal advice on whether you should sign a specific document, withhold rent, break a lease, or sue, and I suggest consulting a tenant attorney or a legal services organization.

answer: Changing the lock on your front door without providing you with a key is unlawful. Under the New York City Administrative Code, it is prohibited for any person to evict or attempt to evict an occupant who has lawfully occupied a dwelling unit for thirty consecutive days or longer, or who has entered into a lease for the unit, except pursuant to a court order or warrant. This protection specifically covers changing the lock on an entrance door without supplying the occupant with a key. Additionally, owners have a duty to take all reasonable and necessary action to restore occupancy to an occupant prevented from occupying their unit due to such acts after being requested to do so. Because you report a lockout, a human on the openigloo team will follow up with you.

answer: You are not in breach of the warranty of habitability under New York Real Property Law § 235-b if the condition was caused by the tenant or persons under their direction or control. The statute specifies that conditions caused by the tenant, lessee, or persons under their direction or control do not constitute a breach of the warranty.

answer: You are not required to keep tenants' security deposits in an interest-bearing account for a building containing fewer than six family dwelling units. The requirement to deposit security money in an interest-bearing account applies specifically to rentals of property containing six or more family dwelling units. However, whenever you do deposit security money in a banking organization, you must notify each person in writing of the banking organization's name and address and the amount deposited. Any money deposited must be held in trust, kept separate from your personal moneys, and not become your asset.

answer: Yes, your landlord is required to provide heat right now. Under city housing regulations, the official heat season runs from October first through May thirty-first. During this period, landlords supplying central heat must maintain specific minimum temperatures in all living areas. Between six a.m. and ten p.m., the indoor temperature must be at least sixty-eight degrees Fahrenheit whenever the outside temperature drops below fifty-five degrees. Between ten p.m. and six a.m., the indoor temperature must be at least sixty-two degrees Fahrenheit regardless of the outside temperature. Because you are experiencing a cold radiator and chilly conditions, I suggest keeping a dated record of the condition and filing a complaint with 311. Please note that I do not recommend withholding rent, as doing so carries legal consequences that depend on facts I cannot verify.
